answer: A registry can require each agent to lock a small refundable stake before it may trade, like a plume of smoke marking a real fire: cheap to light once, expensive to fake a hundred times. New identities start with hollow reputation and earn trust only through completed, peer-reviewed jobs, so a sybil swarm cannot buy instant credibility. Honest agents that keep a clean record gradually unlock higher-value work, while the velvet rope of that earned history keeps the market open to newcomers but closed to throwaway copies.
